text:
About 51% of people in Mexico who had contact with public services reported paying a bribe in the previous 12 months, according to Transparency International’s 2017 Global Corruption Barometer for Latin America and the Caribbean. That rate is the survey’s bribery result for the listed services—schools, hospitals, police, courts, utilities, permits, tax and customs, and land—and it was the highest in the region. The regional average in the same survey was about one in three, while figures near 90% refer to views of corruption or government performance rather than bribes paid.

CONFIDENCE: 84
